subject: Trial validation checklist and evaluation approach for AlliedHealth trial
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karen Miller <kmiller@alliedhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap and next steps — AlliedHealth trial validation checklist

Hi Karen,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment. Quick recap and proposed trial validation checklist so we can get the kickoff scheduled: 

Goal: Validate Redwood inference for AlliedHealth intake triage and: (1) reduce manual triage latency, (2) surface high-confidence routing suggestions to reduce first-touch reassignments.

Summary of outcomes from today:
- AlliedHealth will provide a de-identified sample of ~1,000 recent intake forms (CSV) and a short mapping of your routing labels.
- Legal will confirm NDA via PDF (you mentioned Joe would send).
- Success criteria draft: Macro routing accuracy >= 88% (weighted by volume), precision for urgent labels >= 92%, average human override rate <= 10% during shadow.

Proposed trial plan (high level):
1) Prep (1 week): exchange NDA, sample dataset, sign access terms, S3 share.
2) Offline eval (1 week): Redwood runs batch offline eval on provided sample + our evaluation rubric (precision/recall, confusion matrix, latency distribution).
3) Live shadow (2 weeks): model runs in parallel on live traffic, suggestions visible to agents (no automated routing). Collect human-override metrics and qualitative feedback.
4) Acceptance gate (end of shadow): combination of offline metrics + shadow override targets to decide rollout.

Ownership:
- Redwood: model serving, shadow infra, eval report, runbook for handoff — Marcus will lead SE coordination.
- AlliedHealth: dataset delivery, label mapping, and access for pilot — Karen/Legal to coordinate.

Attachments referenced: allied_trial_dataset_sample.csv (sample), redwood-trial-eval-rubric.pdf (rubric draft), NDA stub.

Immediate asks for AlliedHealth:
- Please confirm NDA arrival and attach the signed copy.
- Share the sample CSV via S3/Drive by EOD Friday if possible.
- Confirm whether the routing labels are stable or if there is a daily label drift (helps sampling).

If that looks good, I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff next Wed (Mar 25) with Marcus and our infra lead.

Thanks,

We’re broadly aligned on the acceptance gates. Can Marcus and your infra lead join the kickoff?

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps — AlliedHealth trial validation checklist

Quick internal notes / proposed additions to rubric before we send final to Karen: 

Proposed offline evaluation split:
- Use a time-based split: last 6 months for training/validation sampling, hold out most recent 4 weeks as "protected holdout" to surface label drift.
- Stratify by label frequency so rare urgent labels have minimum 200 examples in eval set.

Evaluation metrics (additions):
- Macro accuracy weighted by label frequency (target >= 0.88).
- Precision@Top1 for urgent/clinical-critical labels (target >= 0.92).
- Recall for safety-critical categories (target >= 0.85).
- 95th percentile inference latency (target <= 250ms) and 99th percentile for batch spikes.
- Human override rate during shadow (target <= 10%) and net agent time saved (avg sec saved per case).

Grading rubric (scoring):
- Offline pass if metrics meet thresholds on holdout (binary pass/fail).
- Shadow pass if: offline pass AND average override rate <= 10% AND no single-day spike of >20% override.
- Final acceptance requires an internal QA review of 200 flagged cases with at least 80% agreement with human labelers.

Security/logging notes for Karen: we should offer encrypted logs in their VPC S3 with 30-day retention by default; archival options available upon request. Marcus can confirm infra details on the kickoff.

I’ll draft an updated rubric doc (redwood-trial-eval-rubric.pdf) and attach.

—Sergio

Hi Karen / Joe,

Fantastic — thanks for the quick turnaround on the NDA and dataset timing. Per Sergio’s suggestions I’ve updated the rubric and timeline below. Please review and confirm: 

Updated trial timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): NDA signed, sample dataset received, drive/S3 access granted.
- Week 1 (offline eval): Redwood runs batch eval on holdout and sends a full metrics report (incl. 95p latency).
- Weeks 2–3 (shadow, live): Model suggestions surfaced to agents in a read-only view. We’ll collect override metrics and a weekly qualitative notes doc.
- End of Week 3: Acceptance call with stakeholders to review the rubric results and QA sample.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Offline eval report (metrics, confusion matrix, recommended model config).
- Shadow dashboard access (daily override %, per-label breakdown).
- Runbook and rollback plan if you want automated routing off ramp later.

Deliverables from AlliedHealth:
- De-identified CSV sample and label mapping (by Friday).
- One operational contact for agent feedback collection during shadow.

Kickoff: I propose Tue Mar 24 at 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET. Marcus (SE) and our infra lead will join. Confirmable link: https://calendly.com/redwood/alli-trial-kickoff (or propose another time).

Next steps (action owners):
- Karen: share dataset + confirm agent contact (AHT) — due Fri Mar 20 EOD.
- Joe: confirm logging/retention constraint via reply — due Fri Mar 20.
- Marcus: prep shadow infra and invite infra lead to kickoff (internal).
- Sergio: finalize rubric doc and upload to Drive.

Happy to jump on a quick call if anything here needs rework. Looking forward to getting started.
